key_insight: The paper unifies decoder-only LLM inference, token generation, and tool-using agent behavior as a multi-index hybrid dynamical system with distinct fast, slow, and mode-switching dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This framing can help engineers analyze stability, memory/state handling, and tool-trigger policies in agentic LLM systems more rigorously.
method: Models transformer depth as an ultrafast cascade, interpreting layer normalization as spherical projection and KV cache as an exact internal state.
Treats token generation as a stochastic difference process with finite-context truncation yielding a time-homogeneous Markov chain.
Introduces hybrid switching manifolds and jump maps for transitions between generation and tool-execution modes, plus a task-level error process.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates formal derivations of causally invariant KV caching, Markov structure under context truncation, and error bounds under conditional hazard/drift assumptions, but does not report empirical experiments.
watch_item: The framework is highly formal and depends on modeling assumptions that may be difficult to verify or maintain in real LLM-agent deployments.
paper_title: On the Multi-Index, Multi-Rate, and Multi-Phase Dynamics of Decoder-Only Language Models: A Unified Hybrid Framework for Generative and Agentic Systems
